rationale: GABA resolved to CHEMBL96 (SMILES C(CC(=O)O)CN) and ChEMBL records zero measured activities at GPR26 (Q8NDV2), so this exact pair is not already in the pharmacology literature; however GABA is a highly promiscuous, tiny zwitterionic metabolite with 277 affinity measurements across at least 75 distinct targets (GABA-A subtypes, 5-HT3A, D1 dopamine receptor, FFAR3, multiple CYPs), and AF3's ipTM=0.92 with only 370.9 A^2 buried surface is the expected result for a small molecule placed in a GPCR pocket, not evidence of specificity. GPR26 is a brain-enriched orphan Gs-coupled GPCR (UniProt Q8NDV2: "Orphan receptor... significant constitutive activity... mediated by G(s)-alpha"), so a GABA ligand hypothesis is biologically conceivable given the supplied producers SLC6A1/SLC6A11 are GABA transporters also expressed in brain, but nothing here discriminates this receptor from any other pocket.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt Q8NDV2 ptm_topology_feature_counts show only 1 Disulfide bond and no Glycosylation or Lipidation features — the kind of PTM AF3 handles adequately, so no glycan-based artifact concern. pubmed_ptm_glycosylation returned 1 hit (PMID 21924326), a GPR26-knockout mouse behaviour paper about phosphorylated CREB levels, unrelated to receptor PTMs or this interface.
known_interaction_evidence: Not applicable in the protein-protein sense (partner is a metabolite); the small-molecule analogue, chembl_known_activity at Q8NDV2, returned zero records, so the pair is novel in ChEMBL.
ligand_evidence: resolve_small_molecule: GABA -> CHEMBL96, SMILES C(CC(=O)O)CN, InChIKey BTCSSZJGUNDROE-UHFFFAOYSA-N (PubChem fallback). chembl_known_activity at Q8NDV2 (GPR26): 0 activities, 0 affinity measurements — no measured Ki/Kd/IC50/EC50 for this pair. chembl_ligand_promiscuity: 277 affinity measurements over >=75 distinct targets sampled, including GABA-A receptor subtypes, 5-HT3A, D(1A) dopamine receptor, free fatty acid receptor 3 and several cytochrome P450s — a floor, not a total. The small 370.9 A^2 buried surface is modest for a genuine deep orthosteric pose.
follow_up: Run the counter-screen that actually tests specificity: fold GABA against two or three unrelated receptors (e.g. a class-A orphan such as GPR3 plus a non-GPCR control) and show the ipTM/pose quality does NOT reach the same level — a confident pose at GPR26 alone means nothing. In the same fold, read the `ligands` block rather than ipTM: buried_fraction (should be >=0.7 for a real pocket; the supplied 370.9 A^2 BSA is suspiciously small), pocket topology (contacts must fall on Transmembrane segments, with ECL residues, not purely cytoplasmic or purely extracellular-loop), ligand_plddt_mean (>50), and clash/min_separation_A. Wet-lab confirmation would be a cAMP accumulation assay on GPR26-transfected cells (it is constitutively Gs-active, so look for GABA-dependent modulation above the high basal) with GABA-A/GABA-B antagonists present to exclude endogenous receptors.

rationale: ChEMBL records no measured activity of GABA (CHEMBL96) at GPR150 (UniProt Q8NGU9), so the pair is not already known. However, GABA has 277 affinity measurements across at least 75 distinct targets in ChEMBL, many unrelated to GABA receptors (cytochrome P450s, 5-HT3A, dopamine D1A, FFAR3), and it is a very small, flexible zwitterion that AF3 would be expected to place confidently in almost any GPCR pocket. The ipTM of 0.91 is therefore not specific evidence for this receptor; the only support beyond the fold is weak tissue-level overlap of GPR150 with the GABA-producing enzyme GAD2 in brain and pancreas.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt Q8NGU9 lists no Glycosylation or Lipidation features and no PTM-category keywords for GPR150. pubmed_ptm_glycosylation returned 1 hit (PMID 6178845, on visna virus precursor polypeptides), which is unrelated to GPR150. There is no evidence of a receptor modification that would affect the modeled pocket.
known_interaction_evidence: ChEMBL holds no measured affinity for GABA at GPR150 (0 activities at Q8NGU9). UniProt describes GPR150 only as "Orphan receptor" with no known endogenous ligand. STRING, CellPhoneDB and pubmed_cooccurrence were not called because they index protein-protein pairs and do not cover a metabolite against a receptor.
ligand_evidence: resolve_small_molecule returned GABA as CHEMBL96, SMILES C(CC(=O)O)CN, InChIKey BTCSSZJGUNDROE-UHFFFAOYSA-N (source PubChem). chembl_known_activity at Q8NGU9 (target CHEMBL4523898) returned 0 activities. chembl_ligand_promiscuity returned 277 affinity measurements at 75 distinct targets (a floor, since it is counted over a sample of up to 400 measurements), including GABA-A receptor subtypes but also 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 3A, D(1A) dopamine receptor, free fatty acid receptor 3, cytochrome P450 1A2/2C19/2C9/2D6/3A4, arylsulfatase A and ferritin light chain. Supplied fold metrics: ipTM 0.91, ligand pLDDT 78.7, buried surface area 197.8 Å2. No ligands block (buried fraction, pocket topology, clash check) was available, so whether the pose sits in the transmembrane orthosteric site is unverified.
follow_up: fold_complex was not available in this run. Recommended: (1) re-fold GPR150 with GABA (SMILES C(CC(=O)O)CN) and read the ligands block: buried_fraction (should be about 0.7 or above), pocket topology (contacts must be on Transmembrane segments, not Cytoplasmic or extracellular-loop only), ligand pLDDT and clash/min separation; (2) run the specificity counter-screen by folding GABA against two or three unrelated class A GPCRs and comparing ipTM and pose with the GPR150 result; (3) if the pose survives both, test GABA in a GPR150 functional assay (for example beta-arrestin recruitment or cAMP/Ca2+ readout) with GABA-B receptor as a positive control.
